gaps.sentence: 'We might have missed the turning,' he admitted. He admitted that they ___ have missed the turning.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form, so it is unchanged.
'Whether/if' + statement order + 'had' for the present perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'We stayed at this hotel last summer,' they recalled. They recalled that they had stayed at ___ hotel the summer before.
gaps.explanation: Demonstratives shift: this hotel → that hotel; last summer → the summer before.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave now or I'll call the police!' he shouted. He ___ to call the police.
gaps.explanation: A threatening conditional utterance is reported as threatened to do something.

gaps.sentence: "Congratulations!" — She ___ me on passing the exam.
'I was living in Berlin at the time,' she recalled. She recalled that she ___ living in Berlin at the time.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: was living → had been living.

gaps.sentence: 'The road is being resurfaced,' the council said. The council said the road ___ resurfaced.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive (is being resurfaced) backshifts to past continuous passive: was being resurfaced.
